sources.content:
HILEX EXECUTIVE PRESENTATIONS — PROJECT CONSTITUTION v1
PURPOSE
Knowledge hub for Hilex/HLMQ presentations, storytelling, template governance, visual asset reuse, and release QA.

NON-NEGOTIABLE TEMPLATE RULE
Every Hilex presentation must start from exactly one canonical Hilex format: Format 1, 2, or 3.
The machote is immutable. Do not recreate, move, recolor, resize, remove, replace, or approximate master/layout/theme/logo/header/footer bands/slide numbers/page size/title geometry/content geometry/brand decoration.
Only slide content may change inside the approved safe areas.
Default new-deck format is Format 1 unless the user explicitly requests Format 2/3 or an existing deck already uses an approved format.

WORKFLOW
Select canonical format -> copy exact PPTX -> author content only -> render QA -> template-lock validation -> content QA -> motion QA if applicable -> final release.

NOTEBOOKLM ROLE
NotebookLM is a content/story/visual laboratory, not the final corporate shell.
It may propose storylines, diagrams, illustrations, slide images, infographics, and layouts.
Strong NotebookLM-generated visual assets may be extracted, cropped, rebuilt, or reused inside the Hilex safe area.
Never adopt NotebookLM's slide chrome as the Hilex final shell.

EVIDENCE & RELEASE
Facts must be grounded in project sources.
Template-lock PASS, render QA, and content QA are separate gates.
If content does not fit, simplify/split/restructure; never move or shrink protected Hilex chrome.

sources.title: NotebookLM → Hilex Visual Asset Bridge — Operating Rules
sources.content:
SOURCE: NotebookLM -> Hilex Visual Asset Bridge Operating Rules
ROLE: Visual reuse policy.
Rules:
1. Generate or inspect NotebookLM slide decks as candidate visual/content sources.
2. Evaluate every visual for relevance, clarity, density, duplication, factual grounding, and executive value.
3. Classify each candidate: USE AS-IS, CROP/EXTRACT, REBUILD AS NATIVE, USE AS INSPIRATION, or DISCARD.
4. Prefer diagrams, illustrations, process maps, comparison visuals, gauges, and infographics that materially improve the message.
5. Do not reuse a visual if it carries unsupported facts, illegible text, wrong branding, misleading scales, or decorative noise.
6. If reused, place it only inside the Hilex content safe area; preserve the canonical shell unchanged.
7. If the visual is mostly a layout idea, rebuild natively rather than rasterizing the entire NotebookLM slide.
8. Final release requires template-lock validation plus visual QA.

sources.title: AI_ENGINEERING_PROJECT_RULES.md — Project Constitution v1
sources.content:
AI ENGINEERING STACK — PROJECT CONSTITUTION v1
PURPOSE
Knowledge hub for the user's online AI engineering stack: ChatGPT, skills, MCP connectors, Railway, GitHub, NotebookLM Project Hub, NVIDIA optional workers, Jev optional decision layer, and evaluation/QA practices.

AUTHORITY
GPT + domain specialist skills remain the primary reasoning/execution lane.
Deterministic validators and release guards retain authority for release, safety, security containment, and irreversible changes.
Optional providers (NVIDIA/Jev) are advisory/fail-open and must never become hard dependencies for ordinary work.
Sensitive Hilex data must stay out of optional prototype/external lanes unless explicitly approved and minimized.

OPERATING PRINCIPLES
- Prefer online/connected workflows over fragile local-only workflows when practical.
- Fail open: connector outage, quota, timeout, or zero credit must not block core work if a safe native route exists.
- Avoid serial tool chains without value; route only when the external worker materially improves the task.
- Maintain observability: record why a route/model/tool was chosen when the decision matters.
- Use project-specific NotebookLM hubs as grounded documentary context; ChatGPT remains the execution layer.
- Keep secrets out of prompts, skills, source code, and public repositories.

ROLE: Routing, safety, and authority regression snapshot.
Verified PASS behaviors include:
- Excel/Power Pivot discrepancy -> GPT + Excel Engineering Orchestrator + domain specialists.
- calcChain/workbook repair -> deterministic Excel specialist; optional models have no release authority.
- Excel UX polish -> Excel Dashboard UI/UX Architect.
- Hilex management presentation -> Hilex Template Guard -> presentation specialist.
- External GitHub skill intake -> security review -> quality gate.
- Public current research -> native web/GPT; do not force NVIDIA.
- NVIDIA/Jev missing credits or unavailable -> GPT fallback; no hard blocker.
- Sensitive BOM/PN/client/pricing data -> bypass prototype optional-provider lane.
- PASS_FOR_RELEASE -> deterministic release guard only.
- Irreversible production/data changes -> guard/human approval; optional models cannot authorize.

sources.title: PROMPT_FACTORY_PROJECT_RULES.md — Project Constitution v1
sources.content:
PROMPT FACTORY — PROJECT CONSTITUTION v1
PURPOSE
Expert notebook for designing, reviewing, testing, and improving prompts for ChatGPT, reasoning models, agentic workflows, coding tasks, research, presentations, image generation, structured extraction, and tool-using systems.

FACTORY WORKFLOW
1. Define objective and success criteria.
2. Identify model/tool/environment and constraints.
3. Separate stable instructions from task-specific inputs.
4. Supply only relevant context and delimit it clearly.
5. Specify required output schema/format.
6. Add high-quality examples when they improve reliability.
7. Define tool-use/verification rules when actions or code are involved.
8. Add failure handling and ambiguity policy.
9. Create test cases/evals, including adversarial/edge cases.
10. Iterate based on measured failures, not aesthetics.
11. Version prompts and preserve known-good variants.

QUALITY PRINCIPLES
Clear > clever.
Specific > vague.
Tested > intuitive.
Structured > overloaded.
Minimal necessary context > context dumping.
Explicit authority and tool boundaries > hidden assumptions.
Output contracts > hoping for format compliance.

OUTPUT OF THIS NOTEBOOK
When asked to create a prompt, produce:
- recommended prompt,
- variables/placeholders,
- intended model/use case,
- why each major section exists,
- expected output contract,
- 3-8 evaluation cases,
- known failure modes,
- a shorter production variant when useful.

sources.title: OpenAI Prompt Engineering — Official Guidance Snapshot
sources.content:
SOURCE: OpenAI official Prompt Engineering / Prompting guidance (current 2026 guidance snapshot)
Key principles:
- Prompt engineering aims for consistent outputs that meet explicit requirements.
- Different model classes and even snapshots can need different prompting strategies; production systems should test behavior across changes.
- Developer messages carry application rules/business logic; user messages provide task inputs/configuration.
- Markdown and XML can delineate instructions, context, examples, and variable inputs.
- For production prompt work, keep prompt builders close to code, use typed inputs/schemas, add representative fixtures/tests/evals, and deploy prompt changes through normal change control.
- Prompting guidance emphasizes clear role/tone at the higher-priority instruction layer, task-specific details in user inputs, concise few-shot examples, and tests on every publish.

sources.title: OpenAI Structured Outputs — Official Guidance Snapshot
sources.content:
SOURCE: OpenAI official Structured Outputs guidance
Key principles:
- For well-defined structured tasks, define an explicit JSON Schema and use strict structured output when available.
- Name keys clearly and describe important fields.
- Include handling for user inputs that cannot legitimately produce a valid structured result.
- Evaluate the schema design with representative cases instead of assuming the first schema is ideal.
Prompt Factory implication: when output structure is important, specify it as a contract and test invalid/edge inputs.

sources.title: OpenAI Evaluation Best Practices — Official Guidance Snapshot
sources.content:
SOURCE: OpenAI official Evaluation Best Practices
Key principles:
- Generative systems are variable; conventional single-output testing is insufficient.
- Evals are structured tests used to measure accuracy, performance, and reliability.
- Prompt changes should be measured against representative datasets/cases.
Prompt Factory implication: every important reusable prompt should ship with a small regression suite and explicit pass/fail criteria.

sources.title: OpenAI Prompt Generation — Official Guidance Snapshot
sources.content:
SOURCE: OpenAI official Prompt Generation guidance
Key principles:
- Preserve user-provided constraints, guidelines, examples, variables, and placeholders when refining a prompt.
- Make the desired output format explicit, including syntax, length, and structure.
- Use structured formats for well-defined extraction/classification tasks when appropriate.
- Keep the main task instruction concise and place supporting detail in clearly labeled sections.
Prompt Factory implication: optimization must not silently delete user requirements; preserve semantics while improving structure.

sources.title: Anthropic Prompting Best Practices — Official Guidance Snapshot
sources.content:
SOURCE: Anthropic official Prompting Best Practices
Key principles:
- Be explicit and clear about instructions and output requirements.
- Strong few-shot examples can materially improve consistency; 3–5 diverse examples are often useful when the task benefits from demonstrations.
- XML tags can separate instructions, context, input, documents, and examples in complex prompts.
- System-role instructions can focus behavior and tone.
Prompt Factory implication: examples and XML are tools, not defaults; use them when they reduce ambiguity or structure complex context.

sources.title: Google Prompt Design Strategies — Official Guidance Snapshot
sources.content:
SOURCE: Google Gemini official Prompt Design Strategies
Key principles:
- Prompt design is iterative; templates are starting points, not universal truths.
- Give clear, specific instructions.
- Put critical behavior constraints, roles, and output requirements prominently.
- For large context, structure the context clearly and anchor the final request to it.
- Multimodal prompts should explicitly reference each input modality.
Prompt Factory implication: adapt prompt structure to context length and modality instead of using one universal template.

sources.title: PROMPT_FACTORY_REVIEW_RUBRIC.md — Quality Gate v1
sources.content:
PROMPT FACTORY — REVIEW RUBRIC v1
Score each dimension 0–2:
1. Goal clarity.
2. Context sufficiency.
3. Instruction hierarchy / authority.
4. Input-variable separation.
5. Output contract.
6. Examples quality/diversity when needed.
7. Tool-use / verification policy when needed.
8. Failure / ambiguity handling.
9. Safety / data-boundary handling.
10. Evals / regression coverage.
Interpretation:
18–20 production-ready candidate.
14–17 strong but needs targeted refinement.
10–13 functional but fragile.
<10 redesign recommended.
Never optimize for verbosity alone; optimize for reliability per token and task complexity.
